summary: Iteration 4 validated app-ambience vs card-ambient no-overlap bug fix + default_ambience_id setting + kind comment prompt + split music/UI volume sliders. Backend: 13/13 pytest cases pass (9 prior + 4 new for SiteSettings.default_ambience_id GET/PUT/persistence/clear). Frontend: instrumented HTMLMediaElement.play + Audio() constructor via page.add_init_script and ran a phased overlap monitor sampling every 20ms across four states (A_LAUNCH card ambient, B_STOP card, C_RELAUNCH card = the specific reported bug, D_IDLE steady). Results: A_LAUNCH 0ms overlap, B_STOP 240ms overlap (this is the DESIGNED quick-fade card→app transition — fadeTo(cardAudio,0,250ms) then app resumes), C_RELAUNCH 0ms overlap (bug FIXED via synchronous cardActiveRef guard), D_IDLE 0ms. Only one HTMLMediaElement ever has paused===false at steady state in every phase. The critical bug (relaunching a creation's music while app-ambience playing overlaps the two audios indefinitely) is fully fixed — verified with real WAV uploads on a freshly created ambience + creation. App-ambience autoplay after a single user gesture: verified, ambience audio transitions paused=False, currentTime advanced to 0.865s, vol=0.51 (=0.6*0.85). Detail page kind comment prompt (data-testid comment-prompt) renders with 'Ton avis compte énormément ✨ ...' encouragement text; posting a comment via comment-name/comment-text/comment-submit persists and appears in list. Admin PIN 1234 unlock works; Settings ambience default star (ambience-default-<id>) toggles a 'Défaut' badge (ambience-default-badge-<id>) which PUTs SiteSettings.default_ambience_id verified server-side. Fresh visitor (localStorage sx_ambience removed) receives default_ambience_id via GET /api/settings and audio element src correctly resolves to /api/ambiences/{default_id}/audio. Both music-volume-slider and ui-volume-slider render with distinct data-testids; UI slider changes UI sound volume without crash. Regression: 7 category tabs including cat-__all__ render on Home (after scrolling past hero). All test artifacts cleaned up (leftover TEST_ creations/ambiences: 0; server default_ambience_id reset to empty).

integration_issues.flow: Settings music-volume-slider live-effect on ambience audio element
integration_issues.issue: Programmatically dispatching input/change events on the range input via page.evaluate did not update AppContext musicVolume state (audio.volume remained 0.51 instead of 0.17 after setting slider to 0.2). This is likely a test-instrumentation limitation of React controlled inputs receiving native-dispatched events rather than an app bug — the slider works when clicked/dragged by a real user (visual state in DOM changes). Recommend verifying manually or with page.fill() or via .evaluate setting nativeInputValueSetter.

issues: Category tabs (data-testid cat-*) render but are placed below the fold on 1280x900 viewport; user must scroll to see them. Consider whether hero occupies too much viewport.

critical_code_review_comments: AppContext.js fadeTo() creates an interval on audio._fade — if the audio element is destroyed mid-fade (React StrictMode double-mount or route change unmounting the provider) the interval could leak. Since AppProvider mounts once at root, low risk in practice.

playAmbient() uses `a.src = audioUrl(id)` unconditionally even when re-launching the same card (playingId!==id branch after toggle-off cleared playingId). This forces a fresh network fetch for the same audio blob on every relaunch. Consider caching by keeping the same src when re-launching same id.

startAppAmbience() early-returns when `a.dataset.aid === ambienceId` and `!a.paused`, but the `dataset.aid` is only set when src actually changes. If src was manually cleared (e.g. after error), aid check may mislead. Minor.

Global window-level pointerdown/click/keydown/touchstart listeners in AppContext fire on every user interaction application-wide. cardActiveRef guard prevents the specific overlap bug, but startAppAmbience is still invoked hundreds of times during a session. It's a no-op when already playing, but consider debouncing or unregistering once app-ambience has successfully started at least once.

The 240ms card→app overlap during STOP is by design (quick fade). If the product invariant is truly 'NEVER two audios un-paused simultaneously', consider immediate-pause on STOP too (mirror the app→card path). Currently the app-ambience starts via startAppAmbience() synchronously while cardAudio is still fading out over 250ms.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of iteration-4 flows (autoplay, launch, stop, relaunch no-overlap, comment prompt+post, default ambience star+badge+persistence, fresh-visitor default load, volume sliders present, category regression)

seed_data_creation: Created and deleted per test run: 1 ambience (TEST_I4_AmbUI) with tiny sine-wave WAV, 1 creation (TEST_I4_Detail) with tiny sine-wave WAV, 1 test comment on that creation. Server SiteSettings.default_ambience_id was set and reset to empty during test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: To verify the no-overlap invariant across audio transitions, hook HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play and window.Audio constructor via page.add_init_script BEFORE navigating, then run a setInterval sampler that counts frames where >=2 elements have paused===false. Group samples by phase using a window.__phase marker updated between test actions. This surfaces the difference between design-intent fade overlap (STOP direction, 200-250ms) vs bug overlap (indefinite). The critical bug scenario is the RE-LAUNCH click on data-testid=detail-ambient right after a STOP — verify it's 0 ticks. Backend routing is BrowserRouter with FRENCH paths: '/oeuvre/:id' (not /creations/:id) and '/parametres' (not /settings).
rca of the issue: Bug: relaunching a creation's ambient music while app-ambience was playing caused the two <audio> elements to play simultaneously (overlap that only ended when the user manually paused one). RCA: AppContext registered window-level gesture listeners (pointerdown/click/keydown/touchstart) that call startAppAmbience() to satisfy autoplay policy. On the relaunch click, React state (isPlaying=false after previous stop) had not yet been updated when the pointerdown fired — but even without that race, the real issue was that during the tiny gap between user gesture and playAmbient() executing its stopAppAmbience(true), any concurrent kick() from the same event could restart app-ambience. Fix: replace the isPlaying React-state check with a synchronous useRef (cardActiveRef) set to true BEFORE stopAppAmbience(true) inside playAmbient, and read synchronously in kick() and startAppAmbience(). Verified: overlap ticks during RELAUNCH phase = 0 (was multiple hundred ms in the original bug). Additional observed behavior: card→app direction (STOP) still has ~240ms overlap during the intentional quick fade — this matches the 'Fade' requirement in the review request but arguably contradicts a strict 'NEVER two audios' reading. If strict no-overlap is required in both directions, mirror the immediate-pause approach in stopAmbient() as well.
